findings.explanation: postFb() — the function that actually calls the Facebook Send API for every outgoing message — decides whether to retry purely from the HTTP status bucket (4xx vs 5xx/network), never inspecting err.response.data.error.code/error_subcode. Facebook Graph API rate-limit error 613 is returned with a 4xx HTTP status (this repo's own test fixture at tests/page-token-health-script.test.js:587 uses status:400 with code:613), so it falls into the same 'break, no retry' branch as truly permanent errors like invalid recipient or bad params — instead of getting backoff. core/messenger-send-errors.js, which classifies errors for the callers in webhook.js, also only special-cases code 551 (recipient unavailable) and code 10 (outside 24h window); it has no branch for 613. Meanwhile core/credentials/page-token-health.js already has a graphErrorCategory() that correctly buckets code 613 as 'rate_limited' distinct from other 4xx — that logic just isn't reused on the message-send path. Net effect: a 613 rate-limit response on message send fails fast with zero backoff and, in the synchronous request path (core/webhook.js processWebhookRequestEvents, ~line 619), is only console.error'd and the message is dropped with no retry at all.
